result: A hosted run of supply-chain.yml's sbom-vuln job exists and succeeded: run 35799579095 (headSha 8889cf0f019d0a02123e9dc9296d624869e737a6, event push, job databaseId 106986593903, conclusion success), among 10 recent successful runs -- the gap's premise that no run ID was recorded is now settled with a concrete run ID. For local Syft coverage: scanning /usr/lib/python3/dist-packages (the Debian-managed system Python 3.12 site-packages, an external interpreter the baseline runtime-venv scan does not cover) found 61 packages, roughly 2.7x the baseline's combined 23. Scanning /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu (525M of native shared libraries) found only 4 artifacts via `syft scan dir:/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu`: 3 dpkg-attributed packages (gcc-14, libzstd, systemd, all via foundBy=elf-binary-package-cataloger) and one binary-classifier match (an embedded 'python' version string), against 1240 measured .so* files in that directory. FIX ROUND CORRECTION: this low count is NOT evidence that these native libraries lack package-manager metadata -- the host's /var/lib/dpkg/status exists (605997 bytes) and a random 30-file sample of the same directory's .so files is 30/30 (100%) dpkg-owned per `dpkg -S`. `syft scan dir:<path>` scopes its scan root to exactly the given directory, so scanning dir:/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu structurally excludes /var/lib/dpkg/status from the scan and denies Syft its normal deb-manifest attribution path for that directory's files; elf-binary-package-cataloger only recovers the few packages whose binaries carry embedded ELF package notes. The low attribution count is a scoping artifact of how this check invoked syft, not a demonstrated blind spot in Syft's native-library cataloging when package-manager metadata is actually reachable. A full recursive scan of /usr/lib (11G total), which would have included /var/lib/dpkg only if the scan root were raised to include it (it is not under /usr/lib), was attempted but exceeded a 280s bounded timeout and was terminated without output; whether a correctly-scoped scan (root including both the library directory and /var/lib/dpkg) would achieve near-complete attribution was not directly tested here and remains open.

verdict_impact.explanation: Settles the 'no recorded run ID' half of the gap outright with a concrete, verifiable run (supports_incumbent for that half). The wider-scan/native-library-completeness half is now inconclusive, not supports_incumbent: the check's own low attribution count for /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu does not demonstrate a Syft coverage gap, because the scan invocation used (`syft scan dir:/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu`) structurally excludes the dpkg database that a corrected sample check shows 100% of a random 30-file sample from that same directory is actually registered under. Whether Syft would attribute most of these libraries under a scan rooted to include both the library directory and /var/lib/dpkg was not tested (the only broader attempt, scanning all of /usr/lib, timed out). Gap 9's completeness concern is therefore neither confirmed nor refuted by this check as executed.

limitations: The full /usr/lib recursive scan (11G) did not complete within the 280s bounded timeout used here; whole-directory native-library coverage remains untested beyond the /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu subdirectory (525M) and /usr/lib/python3.12 (27M, 0 artifacts -- it is the stdlib, not a site-packages directory) sampled here.

The corrected dpkg-ownership check (30-file random sample, 100% dpkg-owned) establishes that package-manager metadata exists for these native libraries on this host; it does not directly measure what a correctly-scoped Syft scan (one whose root includes /var/lib/dpkg alongside the library directory) would actually attribute -- that scan was not run, so the true native-library attribution rate under a corrected invocation remains unmeasured, not merely assumed to be high.

supply-chain.yml's schedule trigger (cron weekly) and dispatch were not used to force a fresh run for this check; the existing most-recent push-triggered run (35799579095, 2026-09-22) was used as the recorded run ID since one already existed, avoiding an unnecessary duplicate hosted run.
